nodes.label: Dependabot 2-day cooldown vs pnpm minimumReleaseAge
nodes.rationale: pnpm refuses packages younger than 24h (ERR_PNPM_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE_VIOLATION, seen on PR #176). nodes.label: Card-declared input counts
nodes.rationale: Each computable card declares the counts it needs, so no tile-by-tile board model is required. Cerisier C and Montagne C cross two landscapes (Cerisier value = Village tile count; Montagne bonus = adjacent Eau tiles), which the declared-counts shape still accommodates.

nodes.label: Torī reference card (the 16th card)
nodes.rationale: Not an Objectif card but the Torī scoring reference shipped in the same deck; it most likely accounts for the '16 cards' the glossary and scoring doc mention against 15 actual Objectif cards. Its table matches SERIES_SCORE = [0, 0, 2, 4, 7, 10] exactly — nothing to fix in code.

nodes.label: Artiste (player role)
nodes.rationale: 1-4 players, ~30 min, age 10+; turn order is clockwise and the Artiste who painted most recently starts.

nodes.label: Paysage Bambou
nodes.rationale: The only tile type that ever carries a Pinceau icon (7 across the whole tile set).

nodes.label: Carte Objectif
nodes.rationale: One card drawn at random per landscape type at setup, in A/B/C difficulty variants; the rulebook recommends the A set for a first game. The unused cards go back in the box, so the selection is fixed for the whole match.

nodes.label: Décompte des points (end-of-game scoring)
nodes.rationale: Four addends: +X PV for a Parchemin, +2 PV for the Pinceau, the Objectif points of each of the 5 landscapes, and the Torī collection points. This is exactly the shape the module's score entry captures.

nodes.label: Groupe de tuiles adjacentes
nodes.rationale: Two or more adjacent tiles of the same landscape form a group — the unit almost every Objectif card scores against.

nodes.label: Les Roues (tile market)
nodes.rationale: Two wheels hold the available tiles: a tile is takeable if it sits on an arrow slot or is adjacent to an empty space, so removals open up new choices. A wheel is refilled only once fully emptied.

nodes.label: Mode Solo
nodes.rationale: Scores against a simulated opponent board with a difficulty bonus — a compare-to-opponent flow, not the 1-4 players entering their own results the module models.
nodes.source_location: p.8 — Mise en place solo / Comparez votre score

nodes.label: Jeton Parchemin
nodes.rationale: The tile placed at the centre of the big wheel at setup fixes which landscape earns a Parchemin; the stack is 5/4/4/3 at 4 Artistes, 5/4/3 at 3, 5/3 at 2, highest remaining taken first, so the value depends on when it was claimed and how many players there are.

nodes.label: Jeton Pinceau
nodes.rationale: A single physical token: taken by placing a Bambou tile bearing the Pinceau icon, it lets its holder pick any tile around a wheel without restriction, then returns to the centre. Whoever holds it at game end scores +2 PV — hence at most one holder per match.

nodes.label: Plateau Tableau
nodes.rationale: Each Artiste's personal grid, carrying two special spot symbols: the Parchemin spot and the = rows that grant Sceaux.
nodes.source_location: p.6 — Les emplacements des plateaux Tableau

nodes.label: Règles de pose des tuiles
nodes.rationale: First tile must go on the bottom row; a tile on a higher row must be entirely supported by those below it (the board edge counts as support, so 2 tiles suffice in the left and right columns).
nodes.source_location: p.5 — Règles de pose des tuiles

nodes.label: Jeton Sceau
nodes.rationale: One-use special action per landscape (Eau swaps two tiles on a wheel; Bambou places with one support tile fewer; Montagne reserves a tile when a wheel refills; Village draws 3 from the bag and keeps 1; Cerisier swaps a tile at game end). Earned by placing 3 different landscapes on the = rows; max 2 per Artiste.
nodes.source_location: p.6-7 — Les jetons Sceau / Effets des Sceaux

nodes.label: Torī (jeton porte coloré)
nodes.rationale: 5 colors, 7 copies of each, distributed unevenly across Paysage tiles; scored at game end from the collection on the player's Tableau.

nodes.label: Barème des séries de Torī (0/2/4/7/10)
nodes.rationale: A player may score several series of distinct colors, but a given physical Torī can never belong to two series — which is what makes the grouping a combinatorial optimisation. Worked example in the rulebook: 8 Torī → 12 PV (5 distinct + 2 distinct + 1).

nodes.label: Tuile Paysage
nodes.rationale: Five types (Cerisier, Montagne, Bambou, Eau, Village), drawn from a bag onto the wheels and placed on the player's Tableau.

nodes.label: Variante des tuiles Papier
nodes.rationale: Modifies the Tableau's shape with Papier tiles; it changes placement, not the scoring formula, which is why the module does not model it.

nodes.label: Table de score des séries de Torī de couleurs différentes (1→0, 2→2, 3→4, 4→7, 5→10)
nodes.norm_label: table de score des series de tori de couleurs differentes (1→0, 2→2, 3→4, 4→7, 5→10)

nodes.label: Plusieurs séries de Torī peuvent être marquées
nodes.norm_label: plusieurs series de tori peuvent etre marquees

nodes.label: Iconographie des cinq couleurs de Torī (vert triangle, rouge losange, bleu goutte, jaune étoile, violet spirale)
nodes.norm_label: iconographie des cinq couleurs de tori (vert triangle, rouge losange, bleu goutte, jaune etoile, violet spirale)

nodes.label: Neighbour-dependent cards stay manual
nodes.rationale: Village variante A (+4 per neighbouring Tableau with strictly fewer Village tiles) and Eau variante C (+10 if your largest Water group beats every neighbour's) score against the neighbouring players' boards, which needs a seating order the app does not model. They show a short note and a plain total field.

nodes.label: Greedy Torī series grouping
nodes.rationale: 'Peel one of every color still available, repeat' always finds the maximum-scoring grouping and reproduces the rulebook's own worked example (8 Torī → 12 VP), so the user enters raw counts and never has to plan the grouping.

nodes.label: Guided Objectif entry
nodes.rationale: Score entry asks only for the one-to-three counts the selected card actually needs ('how many groups of exactly 2 Bamboo tiles?') and computes points from the card's own table — deliberately avoiding a tile-by-tile board model, since the player still reads the counts off their physical board. 13 of the 15 cards are computed this way.

nodes.label: Per-landscape manual override
nodes.rationale: Every card keeps a 'enter the total by hand' tickbox whose typed value wins — the escape hatch if a transcribed scoring table turns out to be wrong. Un-ticking recomputes from whatever counts were already entered.

nodes.label: Rules deliberately not modeled
nodes.rationale: Sceau effects only change what a player could place during the physical game, never the final tally; the Papier tile variant has no scoring effect; solo mode is a different flow entirely. None of the three earns a score input.

nodes.label: An untouched count reads as zero
nodes.norm_label: an untouched count reads as zero
nodes.rationale: A half-filled card scores what its form actually says rather than falling back to a total the screen never showed; an out-of-bounds count holds that landscape at 0 until corrected.

nodes.label: Winner and tie-break resolution
nodes.rationale: Highest total VP, then total Torī held, then Pinceau possession; an unresolved tie is shared and every tied player is handed rank 1 — carrying into Scoreo's history a rule Scoreo itself does not know.

nodes.label: Règle d'égalité (tie-break)
nodes.rationale: Ties go to the tied Artiste who painted the most Torī, then to whoever holds the Pinceau; an unresolved tie is shared.

nodes.label: Les trois couches (hôte / écran / domaine)
nodes.rationale: Le domaine ne connaît rien, l'écran ne connaît que le domaine et le contrat, l'hôte n'est joignable qu'à travers ModuleHost. Rien ne touche localStorage.

nodes.label: Module de comptage (pas une application)
nodes.rationale: Le paquet n'a ni build, ni déploiement, ni stockage : joueurs, historique, stats, export, thème et persistance restent à l'hôte. Ce que le module possède, c'est le jeu.

nodes.label: ScoringModuleScreenProps (host, playerIds, editing, onExit)
nodes.rationale: Le module ne stocke jamais un nom de joueur, seulement un id : les noms viennent de host.getPlayers(). Rouvrir une partie (editing) gagne toujours sur le brouillon courant.

nodes.label: Documentation 1000 Sabords
nodes.rationale: La doc du jeu vit dans le paquet du module ; ce qui concerne le dépôt entier (build, CI, déploiement, contrat hôte/module) reste dans doc/ à la racine.

nodes.label: index.ts n'exporte que le manifeste et le module
nodes.norm_label: index.ts n'exporte que le manifeste et le module
nodes.rationale: Le registre de Scoreo l'importe de façon eager : tout ce qu'index.ts ré-exporterait voyagerait dans le bundle principal de l'hôte. Le domaine se rejoint par chemin relatif.

nodes.label: Identité visuelle scopée (.module-mille-sabords + préfixe ms-)
nodes.rationale: Les deux, pas l'un ou l'autre : le scoping protège l'hôte du module, le préfixe protège le module de l'hôte. Vérifié statiquement par scripts/check-module-styles.mjs. styles.css est chargé par l'écran, donc voyage dans son chunk : le module arrive stylé et ne coûte rien tant que personne ne l'ouvre.

nodes.label: Le bug d'origine (EtatTour.kt non persisté)

nodes.label: EvenementCoup (union discriminée)
nodes.rationale: Là où le Kotlin avait une sealed class, le TypeScript a une union discriminée sur `type` et la méthode abstraite devient la fonction libre contributionPour().

nodes.label: Repli à zéro (Math.max(0, acc + contribution))
nodes.rationale: Porté par totalJoueurParNom (privée) : sans ce plancher à zéro appliqué à chaque événement, les manches ne somment plus au classement et l'import de Scoreo rejette la partie.

nodes.label: Une instance par état, pas un singleton
nodes.norm_label: une instance par etat, pas un singleton
nodes.rationale: L'app Kotlin partageait un `val partie` global. L'agrégat est mutable : le garder dans l'état du réducteur ferait dépendre sa sortie de qui d'autre en détient une référence. L'écran garde donc le journal et rejoue l'agrégat via partieDeLEtat(state).

nodes.label: Event sourcing (journal d'EvenementCoup)
nodes.rationale: Chaque action de jeu est un EvenementCoup stocké dans l'historique ; les totaux se dérivent du journal au lieu d'être stockés à côté.

nodes.label: L'agrégat Partie est délibérément absent de l'état
nodes.norm_label: l'agregat partie est deliberement absent de l'etat
nodes.rationale: L'agrégat est mutable : en garder un dans l'état ferait dépendre la sortie du réducteur de qui d'autre en détient une référence. C'est la traduction du `val partie` global du Kotlin : ce que le singleton portait, le journal le porte, sans le partager.
